name: TeXstudio
product: TeXstudio by the TeXstudio project

evidence.says: The project lists a dedicated macOS M1 archive for TeXstudio 4.9.10 and dates the release November 20, 2026.

notes: The project lists separate Mac downloads and specifies macOS 13 or later.

name: PyMOL
product: Incentive PyMOL by Schrödinger

evidence.says: Schrödinger labels the current 3.1.9 Mac DMG as Apple Silicon, dates the update October 7, 2026, and links separately to Intel downloads.

name: BetterDiscord
product: BetterDiscord Installer by the BetterDiscord project

evidence.says: The project describes the downloadable utility as an installer, remover and maintenance program for BetterDiscord.
The installation guide verifies the resulting BetterDiscord features inside Discord itself.

notes: The scanned identifier belongs to the installer for a Discord modification.

name: LogMeIn Hamachi Installer
product: LogMeIn Hamachi Installer by LogMeIn (GoTo)

evidence.says: LogMeIn's instructions distinguish the installer launched on Mac from the Hamachi client it installs.
The cask identifies LogMeInHamachiInstaller.app as an installer artifact.

notes: The Hamachi client merits a separate listing under its own bundle ID.

name: Install
product: Drobo Dashboard Installer by Drobo, Inc.

evidence.says: Drobo's 5D3 user guide identifies Install.app inside the Drobo Dashboard disk image as the installer for the Mac dashboard.

notes: The bundle is the Install.app used to install Drobo Dashboard.

name: Creality_Print
product: Creality Print, Creality's 3D printer slicer

evidence.says: Creality published the v7.3.2 release on November 13, 2026.
Creality ships separate macOS arm64 and x86_64 DMGs for build 7.3.2.6412.

name: SecureCRT
product: VanDyke Software SecureCRT terminal client for macOS

evidence.says: VanDyke's November 3, 2026 release lists a standalone SecureCRT 9.7.4 build 4010 arm64 DMG for Apple Silicon Macs.

name: RobloxPlayerInstaller
product: Roblox Corporation's macOS installer for Roblox Player

evidence.says: Roblox describes installing the player and then opening the installed Roblox.app to play on a Mac.
Roblox offers the Mac app through its official download page.

notes: The scanned app is the installer bundle; the installed Roblox Player is a separate listing.

name: 1cv8s
product: 1C:Enterprise 8 interactive launcher by 1C Company

evidence.says: The vendor identifies 1cv8s as the version-specific interactive launcher that selects an infobase and starts the corresponding 1C:Enterprise client.

notes: The listing is for the launcher component of the 1C:Enterprise suite.

name: Apifox
product: Apifox desktop API development and testing platform by Apifox

evidence.says: Apifox lists separate Apple Silicon and Intel downloads for the macOS desktop client.
The live cask identifies the 2.8.55 Apple Silicon app download as the vendor-hosted Apifox-macOS-arm64-2.8.55.dmg.

limitation: The stable release date was not established.

name: SpringToolSuite4
product: Spring Tools for Eclipse, formerly Spring Tool Suite 4, by the Spring Tools team (Broadcom)

evidence.says: Spring lists a macOS ARM_64 download for the standalone Spring Tools for Eclipse 5.4.0 distribution.
The Spring Tools team announced the Eclipse distribution of 5.4.0 on September 9, 2026.

notes: The listing covers the standalone Eclipse distribution.

name: Retroactive (right click to open)
product: Retroactive by Shawn Cormierty

evidence.says: Retroactive 3.0 restores support for newer macOS releases and discusses the Rosetta 2 requirement for the older Apple apps it enables.
Static inspection of Retroactive.app/Contents/MacOS/Retroactive in the official 3.0 ZIP found one x86_64 Mach-O slice.
The Homebrew cask identifies Retroactive 3.0 as an Intel build that requires Rosetta 2 on Apple Silicon.

limitation: Compatibility of individual legacy Apple apps depends on the macOS version and hardware.
notes: Version 3.0 supersedes the earlier discontinuation notice for 2.1.

name: WSJT-X
product: WSJT-X by the WSJT development group, originated by Joe Taylor (K1JT)

evidence.says: The official project lists 3.0.2 as the general availability release dated June 18, 2026 and provides separate Apple Silicon and Intel macOS downloads.
The official 3.0.2 release assets include wsjtx-3.0.2-arm64-macOS.pkg.

notes: This is the main WSJT-X project for amateur-radio digital modes.

name: RobloxStudio
product: Roblox Studio by Roblox Corporation

evidence.says: Roblox's Mac Studio version endpoint identifies version 0.748.0.7481526 as build c5c97d45b6614310.
Homebrew links version 0.748.0.7481526 for Apple Silicon to the corresponding arm64 ZIP hosted on Roblox's CDN.
Roblox confirms that Studio has a native Apple Silicon build and sends it to Apple Silicon machines via updates.

notes: The designation applies to RobloxStudio.app.

name: mpv
product: mpv macOS application bundle by the mpv project

evidence.says: The official stable release lists arm64 macOS downloads for macOS 15, 26 and 27.
GitHub records publication on November 5, 2026 and lists the corresponding macOS arm ZIP files.

notes: Upstream now publishes its own stable macOS builds.

name: Sky X
product: Sky X streaming player by Sky Österreich

evidence.says: Sky Österreich announced on September 30, 2026 that it was migrating Sky X customers to WOW and directing them to install the WOW app.
The former Sky X site now redirects visitors to WOW.
The uploaded version 24.1.3-2 from 2024 is recorded as 64-bit Intel.

limitation: The final Sky X desktop version and its architecture could not be established.
notes: WOW succeeded Sky X in Austria.

name: DjVu2PDF
product: DjVu2PDF by majimakHARU

evidence.says: Apple's metadata matches bundle ID com.majimakHARU.DjVu2PDF and reports version 1.4.1 released on October 6, 2026.
The App Store lists 1.4.1 as a maintenance update and specifies macOS 12 or later without stating a processor architecture.

limitation: No architecture declaration or official binary suitable for inspection was found for 1.4.1.
notes: The App Store now distributes a newer release than the 1.3 scan.

name: launcher
product: AssaultCube Mac launcher by the AssaultCube project

evidence.says: The uploaded AssaultCube bundle's plist identifies its executable as launcher and its bundle ID as assaultcube.
The game's own release history identifies the Mac app launcher as part of AssaultCube.

notes: The source scan identifies the launcher inside AssaultCube.app. Any game listing would need evidence for the game executable itself.

name: Aurora HDR
product: Aurora HDR 2019 by Skylum, formerly Macphun

evidence.says: Skylum says Aurora HDR no longer receives updates and identifies Luminar as its replacement.
Homebrew documents the remaining Aurora HDR 2019 build 1.0.2 (6495) as Intel macOS software requiring Rosetta 2 on Apple Silicon.

limitation: The release date and behavior on recent macOS versions were not verified.
notes: The remaining Intel build was not Apple Silicon native.

name: PCSX2
product: PCSX2 PlayStation 2 emulator by the PCSX2 project

evidence.says: The project labels v2.8.2 its latest stable release and includes a macOS build.
The versioned release workflow uploads the default macOS build and omits the separate ARM cache job's artifacts.
The release workflow's default macOS architecture is x86-64.
The official requirements state that PCSX2 runs on M-series Macs through Rosetta 2.

notes: This record covers the upstream stable release.

name: CZUR Aura
product: CZUR Aura desktop scanner software by CZUR Tech

evidence.says: CZUR’s original manual tells Mac users to install the dedicated CZUR Aura app for the hardware.
The current Aura Pro support page offers the unified CZUR Scanner and beta CZUR Image+ installers in place of the former dedicated software.
CZUR describes its unified scanner software as Apple Silicon-native and includes Aura hardware among the supported series.
The exact CZUR Aura 3.1.5 bundle, build 166, is recorded as a 64-bit Intel executable.

limitation: The vendor site has switched distribution to the unified app, but no formal retirement notice or independently dated final CZUR Aura build was found.
notes: The last identified dedicated Aura build is Intel-only. The vendor now offers Apple Silicon-native CZUR Scanner 5.5.5 for Aura hardware.

name: Sunsama
product: Sunsama Desktop by Sunsama

evidence.says: Sunsama distributes its official desktop app for macOS.
Homebrew's live metadata selects the Sunsama 3.5.7 arm64-mac ZIP hosted by the app's ToDesktop distributor for Apple Silicon.

limitation: The release date was not independently published in the sources checked.
notes: The Apple Silicon package uses ToDesktop build 2611250p0w2s765.

name: StagePlotPro 2.9.9.2
product: StagePlotPro by Chip Wallace (Divertisma bundle ID)

evidence.says: Tourouter's October 2026 survey identifies 2.9.9.2 as the last listed desktop version and reports that the original vendor no longer sells it.
MacUpdater identifies Chip Wallace's exact bundle and records release 2.9.9.2 on March 9, 2020 as Intel.

limitation: The final build's Intel architecture was reported by MacUpdater and was not independently inspected.
notes: The similarly named web apps use separate products and vendors.

name: Eponyms
product: Eponyms for Mac by Pascal Pfiffner and Andrew Yee

evidence.says: Apple's metadata matches bundle ID org.bitbucket.p2.maceponyms and lists 1.1 from April 4, 2011 as the current Mac release.
The uploaded Mac 1.1 bundle with this identifier contains only 32-bit and 64-bit Intel slices.

limitation: No vendor statement or credible runtime report was found for this Mac build under Rosetta 2.
notes: The separate mobile Eponyms listing has a different store ID.

name: Adobe Digital Editions
product: Adobe Digital Editions by Adobe

evidence.says: Adobe distributes a Mac installer for version 4.5.12.
The compatibility database records 4.5.12 as Intel-only, with over 100 installations reported.
Adobe says Wipro assumed support, maintenance and new releases for its e-book platform.

limitation: Reports establish translated execution, but end-to-end compatibility with e-readers and DRM workflows varies.
notes: Adobe transferred ongoing support and releases to Wipro. ByteBooks credentials are required for new authorizations.

name: HEY
product: HEY desktop email and calendar client by 37signals

evidence.says: 37signals' Mac update manifest lists HEY 1.3.10, its arm64 ZIP, and a November 20, 2026 release date.
Static inspection confirmed HEY.app/Contents/MacOS/HEY is arm64 and its bundle metadata identifies com.hey.app.desktop version 1.3.10.

name: Screen Snake
product: Screen Snake by Bruno Vandekerkhove (Korion)

evidence.says: Apple's US catalog returns no record for the original Mac App Store ID, and corresponding lookups in seven other storefronts also returned no listing.
MacUpdate lists 5.3 as the last cataloged version.
The archived scan identifies Bruno Vandekerkhove and records only 32-bit and 64-bit Intel slices for version 5.3.

limitation: No developer shutdown announcement or Rosetta 2 runtime report was found.
notes: The original App Store page is gone and no current official download surfaced.

name: Chicken
product: Chicken VNC client by Dustin Aue and the Chicken project

evidence.says: The original project identifies Chicken as a VNC client and records its last project update in January 2016.
The newest original project binary is Chicken-2.2b2.dmg, dated November 19, 2011.
The 2.2b2 executable in the uploaded bundle has only 32-bit slices and no arm64 slice.
The project forum identifies the later 2.2b3 binary as Andreas Böckler's independent GitHub build.

limitation: The project still hosts old files and no explicit end-of-maintenance announcement was found.
notes: The final original project release 2.2b2 was not native.

name: feedly
product: Feedly for Mac by DevHD (Feedly Inc.)

evidence.says: The original launch coverage identifies DevHD's desktop Mac App Store product as item 865500966.
Apple's catalog returned zero results for the original desktop app ID, with the same result in Canada and Turkey.
The exact legacy app's existing scan records bundle version 1.1, build 2, with an x86 executable.

limitation: The release date and any formal retirement announcement were not found.
notes: The current Feedly Smart News Reader store listing is the iPhone and iPad product under a different App Store ID.

name: JView
product: JView image viewer by Allan Liu

evidence.says: Allan Liu's archived release page dates JView 2.1.1 to May 14, 2006 and offers Intel, PowerPC and Universal builds.
The scanned bundle identifies its executable as JView and names Allan Liu in its 2006 copyright.
The current catalog points JView 2.1.1 users to the archived original developer page.

limitation: The original distribution now survives in an archive, and no current official release or Rosetta test was found.
notes: The final known release's Universal build covered Intel and PowerPC.

name: Essential Keyboard Collection
product: SONiVOX Essential Keyboard Collection standalone instrument by SONiVOX (inMusic)

evidence.says: SONiVOX announced end of life for its software products and says it has ended updates and support for new operating systems.
SONiVOX names Essential Keyboard Collection as discontinued software with no support on Sequoia and places the last qualified release on macOS 10.8 through 13.
SONiVOX lists Essential Keyboard Collection as non-native on M1 and confirms Rosetta support in guidance that covers standalone mode.

limitation: SONiVOX does not name the final standalone build version or date in its end-of-life and compatibility notices.
notes: The vendor confirmed Rosetta operation on Apple Silicon with Big Sur and qualified its final software only through macOS 13.

name: Age of Empires III
product: Age of Empires III original Mac OS X port by MacSoft

evidence.says: MacSoft's distributor lists its 1.0.6 Mac patch on September 2, 2011 and describes a Mac OS X Lion compatibility fix.
An owner of the MacSoft port reports that the game is 32-bit and stopped working after upgrading to macOS Catalina.
Apple confirms that 32-bit Mac apps are incompatible with Catalina and later releases.

limitation: The final Mac executable was not inspected directly.
notes: The original MacSoft port predates Age of Empires III: Definitive Edition.

name: MEGAcmd
product: MEGAcmd for macOS by MEGA

evidence.says: Static inspection of the official DMG found megacmd.mac version 2.8.0 and x86_64 plus arm64 slices in MEGAcmd.app/Contents/MacOS/mega-cmd.
MEGA documents mega-cmd as the interactive shell and points Mac users to its official download site.

limitation: The official DMG carries version 2.8.0, while the Homebrew catalog still shows 2.7.1; no 2.8.0 release date was found.
notes: The bundle's CFBundleExecutable is a shell launcher that selects arm64 on Apple Silicon and invokes the universal mega-cmd executable.

name: silex-desktop
product: Silex Desktop 2 (Electron edition) by Silex Labs

evidence.says: Silex Labs identifies 2.7.30 as the stable desktop release; inspection of its DMG matched com.electron.silex-desktop and found an x86_64-only silex-desktop.app/Contents/MacOS/silex-desktop executable.
The newer 2.7.33 package is marked as a prerelease.
The former desktop repository is read-only and directs ongoing development of the Tauri-based desktop project to the Silex monorepo.
Silex offers a separate Apple Silicon installer for the current desktop project.

limitation: The later 2.7.33 prerelease's architecture was not verified.
notes: Silex Labs now distributes a separate Tauri-based alpha with its own Apple Silicon download.

name: Popcorn-Time
product: Popcorn Time's original NW.js desktop client, formerly maintained in popcorn-official/popcorn-desktop

evidence.says: The original desktop repository URL redirects to the Popcorn Time project that now hosts the rebuild.
The maintainers describe the current project as a complete rebuild and designate it as the home of ongoing development and releases.
A historical report links the original project's official macOS arm64 ZIP for the NW.js 0.5.1 release.
A downstream fork preserves a 0.5.1 release with an osxarm64 ZIP.

limitation: The original 0.5.1 release assets are no longer listed on the official repository and its original release date was not confirmed.
notes: The final legacy 0.5.1 release offered a native arm64 build as well as Intel builds.

name: AnkerMake Studio
product: Anker Innovations' AnkerMake Studio FDM slicer, now branded eufyMake Studio 3D

evidence.says: Anker's slicer release notes document the rename from AnkerMake to eufyMake with existing services continuing.
Anker explicitly directs owners of its M5 and M5C FDM printers to the dedicated eufyMake Studio 3D app.
Static inspection of the official 3D DMG found version 1.5.27_E1.8.0 and a single x86_64 slice in eufyMake Studio 3D.app/Contents/MacOS/eufyStudio.
A user shows the macOS translation deprecation alert while using eufyMake Studio 3D.

limitation: The exact release date and the version in the runtime report were not supplied.
notes: The FDM app's bundle identifier changed to com.anker.eufystudio3d/; the UV-focused eufyMake Studio download is separate.

name: Air Display Host
product: Air Display Host by Avatron Software

evidence.says: Avatron calls version 3.4.2 its current Intel-based Mac host and explicitly says it is incompatible with M1 Macs.
The official host update feed dates version 3.4.2 build 26581 to July 12, 2020.

limitation: Avatron specifically tested or addressed M1 Macs in the download notice; compatibility with later Apple Silicon generations was not independently verified.
notes: The host app is the Mac-side display utility. The same-numbered Air Display client uses a different bundle ID.

name: Nudge
product: Nudge Notifier by Amber Sahdev

evidence.says: The official install page links Nudge.zip as version 1.8 and publishes its checksum.
Static inspection of the checksum-matching Nudge.zip found the exact bundle ID and x86_64-only Mach-O files for Nudge.app/Contents/MacOS/Nudge and its bundled Python runtime.
Amber Sahdev's portfolio links Nudge to Nudge Notifier's official domain.

limitation: No firsthand report or vendor statement confirmed Rosetta operation for this release.
notes: The vendor labels the package 1.8, while its internal Info.plist reports 0.0.0. Homebrew's MacAdmins Nudge cask is a separate product.

name: Zenmap
product: Zenmap by the Nmap Project, the official Nmap graphical front end

evidence.says: Nmap's versioned changelog dates 7.993 to October 23, 2026.
The Nmap Project offers 7.993 as an x86-64 macOS installer that includes Zenmap.
Static inspection found the matching org.insecure.Zenmap 7.993 bundle and x86_64-only headers for Contents/MacOS/Zenmap, zenmap.bin, and the bundled python3.

limitation: Zenmap 7.993 runtime under Rosetta 2 was not verified.
notes: The official Zenmap.app is installed from the Nmap disk image.

name: Valentina Studio
product: Valentina Studio by Paradigma Software

evidence.says: Paradigma's Mac App Store release history lists 17.5.3 as the current release and dates the introduction of native Apple Silicon support to 12.5.3.
Apple's live catalog returns the exact scanned bundle ID as Valentina Studio 17.5.3, released August 1, 2026.
Paradigma lists both Intel and ARM64 as supported Mac architectures for Valentina Studio.
Paradigma separately announced Valentina Studio 18.4.1 for direct distribution.

limitation: This finding covers the current Mac App Store build. The newer direct-download release was not inspected.
notes: Native support first appeared in 12.5.3, after the scanned 12.3.2 build.
